Have You Lost Cryptocurrency to an Online Scam?

Cryptocurrency fraud can happen through fake investment platforms, fraudulent exchanges, impersonation, phishing, romance scams, unauthorized transfers, and other online schemes.

Online Fraud Fighter Team helps victims organize what happened, preserve important evidence, review available transaction information, and understand legitimate options for reporting and recovery. Recovery is never guaranteed, and no legitimate service can promise that stolen cryptocurrency will automatically be returned.

Frequently Asked Questions About Cryptocurrency Fraud

Answers to common questions about cryptocurrency fraud investigations, evidence preservation, transaction review, and legitimate recovery options.

Can you guarantee cryptocurrency recovery?

No. Cryptocurrency recovery is never guaranteed. A legitimate investigation can help organize evidence, review transaction information, and identify reporting or recovery options, but no service can honestly promise that stolen funds will be returned.

What information should I provide?

Useful information can include transaction IDs or hashes, wallet addresses, screenshots, emails and messages, payment records, website addresses, names or usernames used by the scammer, dates, amounts, and a clear timeline of what happened. Do not send private keys, seed phrases, passwords, or authentication codes.

Can you trace a cryptocurrency transaction?

Blockchain transactions are often publicly visible and may be reviewed using available transaction and wallet information. Tracing can help identify movement of funds or relevant addresses, but it does not by itself prove who controls a wallet or guarantee that funds can be recovered.

What should I do if a recovery scammer contacts me?

Stop sending money or cryptocurrency, preserve the messages and payment records, and be cautious about anyone demanding upfront fees while promising guaranteed recovery. Never provide private keys, seed phrases, passwords, or authentication codes.

Should I send more cryptocurrency to recover my funds?

No. Be extremely cautious about requests for additional cryptocurrency, taxes, unlock fees, verification payments, or other charges that are presented as a condition for guaranteed recovery. Sending more money can increase your losses.

How long can an investigation take?

The timeframe depends on the complexity of the incident, the amount of evidence available, the number of transactions involved, and the organizations that may need to be contacted. There is no reliable universal timeline or guaranteed recovery deadline.

What types of cryptocurrency scams do you investigate?

Common cases include fake investment platforms, fraudulent exchanges, phishing, impersonation, romance scams, unauthorized transfers, fake recovery services, and other online schemes involving cryptocurrency or digital assets.

A Clear, Evidence-Based Approach

Our approach focuses on organizing available information, preserving evidence, and helping clients understand legitimate next steps. We aim to communicate clearly about what can and cannot be established from the available information.

Evidence First

We encourage clients to preserve transaction IDs, wallet addresses, screenshots, communications, payment records, and other relevant evidence.

No Guaranteed Recovery Claims

Cryptocurrency recovery is never guaranteed. We do not promise that lost or stolen assets will automatically be returned.

Protect Your Credentials

Do not share private keys, seed phrases, passwords, authentication codes, or other sensitive account credentials with anyone claiming they can recover your funds.

Watch for Recovery Scams

Be cautious of anyone demanding additional cryptocurrency or payment while promising guaranteed recovery, immediate refunds, or special access to your funds.

Important: If you believe you have been defrauded, preserve your evidence and avoid sending additional money to a person or service promising guaranteed recovery.
